note: Intrinsic physiology added to the Shiu et al. LIF: spontaneous activity (membrane noise + resting offset calibrated to a target in-vivo spontaneous rate) and spike-frequency adaptation (AdEx-style adaptation current, target adaptation index = steady-state / onset rate for a step that first drives the neuron to 100 Hz). Rules are matched top to bottom; the first match wins. basis per rule given in 'basis'. Edit freely; rebuild with tools/build_physiology.py.

noise.basis: approximate: in-vivo membrane-potential fluctuations of a few mV in fly central neurons (e.g. Gouwens & Wilson 2009 J Neurosci for AL neurons); OU noise

adaptation.basis: approximate: adaptation time constants of hundreds of ms in fly ORNs/PNs (Nagel & Wilson 2011 Nat Neurosci; Bhandawat et al. 2007 Nat Neurosci)

rules.basis: literature: giant fibre is silent at rest and follows high frequencies without adaptation (von Reyn et al. 2014 Nat Neurosci; Tanouye & Wyman 1980)
literature: APL is non-spiking/graded (Papadopoulou et al. 2011 Science); no spontaneous spikes here
literature: escape/flight motor neurons are quiescent at rest and fire only with giant-fibre or flight drive (Tanouye & Wyman 1980; von Reyn et al. 2014)
excluded: optic lobe/photoreceptors are driven by the eye, FlyVis and the graded optic-lobe model
measured: per-receptor spontaneous rate from DoOR (MÃ¼nch & Galizia 2016; Hallem & Carlson 2006; de Bruyne et al. 2001), class median where missing; adaptation approximate (Nagel & Wilson 2011)
literature-approximate: GRN spontaneous activity is low, ~0-2 Hz (Hiroi et al. 2002 Chem Senses)
literature: uniglomerular PNs fire spontaneously at a few Hz (Wilson et al. 2004 Science; Bhandawat et al. 2007)
literature-approximate: spiking AL local neurons (Seki et al. 2010 J Neurophysiol)
literature: Kenyon cells are nearly silent at rest (Turner et al. 2008 J Neurophysiol: <0.5 Hz) and adapt strongly
literature: MBONs fire tonically at several Hz (Hige et al. 2015 Neuron)
literature-approximate: LH neurons fire spontaneously at a few Hz (Fisek & Wilson 2014 Nat Neurosci)
approximate: motor neurons largely quiet at rest; weak adaptation
approximate default: sparse baseline activity across the central brain and nerve cord
